beats: Hook (line_qc_css_three_hoops, then the cover): a 1950 code from Bell Labs fixes any single flipped bit among seven. Use it twice, once for flips and once for signs, and you get a seven-qubit quantum code, but only if the two copies get along. The Hamming code drawn as three overlapping hoops with seven dishes: each hoop must hold an even number of pebbles; one flipped bit upsets exactly the hoops it sits in, and that pattern names the dish (code draws the pebbles). Same cast as QC08-05: the keeper and the imp. No portrait of Hamming, Steane, Calderbank or Shor.

Classical linear codes (Q24-11 66:37-73:22): a generator G makes the codewords, a parity-check matrix H gives Hx = 0 for every codeword, and He is the syndrome that points at the error; the repetition code's two parity checks map one to one onto the Z checks Z1Z2, Z2Z3 (Q25-11 63:40-65:00, clip 64:30-65:00; reuse line_qc_synd_read_bulbs). Skip the screen-share trouble at Q24-11 68:40-69:20.
The Hamming [7,4,3] code (Q24-11 73:22-73:45; Q25-11 65:00-65:40): four data bits, three checks, fixes one flip. Tape Q24-11 s22 and s24.

CSS (Q25-11 63:05-65:59; Q24-11 73:58-74:52): each check is all Z or all X; one classical code becomes the Z checks (round lens: they catch bit flips), a second becomes the X checks (square lens: they catch phase flips); Steane uses the Hamming code for both (line_qc_css_twin_boards; QC08-03's glasses).

They must commute, and that is not automatic (65:59-67:42; Q24-11 76:36-77:29): every X check must overlap every Z check on an even number of qubits; the Hamming checks happen to (four overlaps, two overlaps) (line_qc_css_gears_mesh: gears that mesh vs gears that jam).

Steane [[7,1,3]] beats Shor [[9,1,3]] at the same distance (67:17-67:42; reuse line_qc_min_three_rafts from QC08-06), yet the strategy is not always the best: five qubits is the minimum (clip Q24-11 74:52-75:17). Tape Q25-11 s25 (crop the footer).

Wiring (Q24-11 74:52-76:36, clip 75:43-76:36): a weight-4 Hamming check needs one helper linked to four qubits scattered across the chip; chips link only neighbours, so hardware-aware codes followed: the surface code (each check touches four neighbours) and low-density parity-check codes (line_qc_css_rooftop_strings; reuse line_qc_string_village and line_qc_surf_quilt_knots).

Codes with k > 1 (Q25-11 41:49-42:16, which names a company: keep it off screen): high-rate qLDPC codes hold many logical qubits in one block (line_qc_css_ferry_rowboats). FACTS before any number: e.g. a [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code (2024) against twelve distance-12 surface-code patches; name no company.
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_07; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the keeper between two identical three-hoop patterns, round glasses towards one, square glasses towards the other.

In each of the seven regions sits one small empty round dish. The keeper (an invented young woman with a simple round face and dot eyes, chin-length straight hair held back on one side by a single plain hair clip, a plain one-piece zip-up work overall with the sleeves rolled up and a small torch clipped to its chest pocket, and sturdy work boots) kneels at the lower right edge and points into the middle region; the imp (an invented small mischievous creature, about knee-high to an adult: a round, bean-shaped body, a simple round face with dot eyes and a wide cheeky grin, two big pointed ears sticking out sideways, thin arms and legs, small three-fingered hands and a thin curly tail; drawn in clean outline only: no fur, no horns, no claws, no teeth) peeks out from behind the top hoop.
